business_scope.primary_industry_name: Single-Origin Green Arabica Coffee Bean Container Distribution

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Switzerland; the AG will select its registered seat in a commercial canton (Zurich, Zug or Geneva preferred for commodity trading and trade finance)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (hybrid Germanic-Romance codification; Swiss Civil Code and Code of Obligations are the statutory core, with cantonal procedural variations)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: EFTA Convention (Vaduz, 2001); WTO GATT framework for green coffee trade

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA/GwG) of 10 October 1997, SR 955.0; Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220) arts. 613a et seqq., 620, 626a and 927 et seqq. as amended by the Federal Act of 22 December 2023 establishing the central UBO register (ZRwB/READE); Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV, SR 221.411); FINMA Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance (AMLO-FINMA, SR 955.033); Embargo Act (SR 946.231) and SECO consolidated sanctions ordinances; MROS suspicious-activity reporting under AMLA art. 9.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Deed of incorporation and notarized articles of association (Statuten) of the Swiss AG
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss public notary of the canton of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Not required for the Swiss deed itself; any foreign underlying instrument annexed to the deed requires Hague Apostille or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss commercial bank where the AG share capital account is held
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Not required - Swiss domestic bank certificate subject to notarial inspection

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign corporate extract, certificate of incumbency and good standing for each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the shareholder home state (e.g., Kenya BRS, Colombia Camara de Comercio, Ethiopia Ministry of Trade)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille from the state of issue; Swiss consular legalization for non-Hague Convention states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal-record clearance (Strafregisterauszug) and debt-enforcement certificate (Betreibungsregisterauszug) for each natural-person director and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Fedpol / cantonal criminal records authority and cantonal debt enforcement office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Not required - Swiss domestic certificates; foreign equivalents require apostille or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copies and proof of residential address (UBO piercing identification pack)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-state notary or Swiss diplomatic mission
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Swiss consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Audit-waiver declaration (Verzicht auf die ordentliche Revision) and name-reservation receipt
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Cantonal commercial register office and shareholders' meeting minutes annexed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Not required - Swiss domestic instrument; commercial register issues certified true copies

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, UBOs and material commercial counterparties against the consolidated SECO sanctions list, UN Security Council measures, EU restrictive measures and OFAC SDN list; PEP identification per AMLA art. 2a and AMLO-FINMA art. 12 with FINMA Circular 2023/01 due-diligence governance is required for natural persons from coffee-origin third countries; zero-tolerance for sanctioned regimes and for misdeclared green coffee origins; documentary letters of credit are subject to transaction-level AML/CFT and trade-based money-laundering checks.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix - central business name index (www.zefix.ch); E-CRIS online applications (www.e-cris.ch); cantonal commercial register office (Handelsregisteramt) of the registered office canton
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Art. 944 OR: the firm name may be in any official Swiss language (German, French, Italian, Romansh) or may include a supplementary non-official language such as English if accompanied by an official-language variant; Latin-script transliteration is mandatory for foreign elements; the name must be true, not misleading and distinguishable from existing names; German form recommended for coffee trading, e.g., Green Coffee Import AG, with an optional French/Italian variant.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Swiss - Suisse - Schweiz - Svizzera (requires IPI Swissness authorization)
Eidgenossenschaft - Confederation - Bundes- (reserved for state entities)
Trust - Treuhand (misleading absent fiduciary licence in the relevant canton)
Names contrary to public order and morality under art. 951 OR
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection by the cantonal registrar (based on OR arts. 944-950 and HRegV art. 5), the applicant may, within 10 working days, file a written administrative objection with the cantonal supervisory authority over the commercial register (e.g., Cantonal Department of Economic Affairs); if rejected, the applicant may appeal to the competent Cantonal Administrative Court and ultimately to the Federal Administrative Court for issues of federal law; in parallel, the applicant may file a new name-reservation application with a modified trade name or seek the prior written consent of the conflicting name holder.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partial and conditioned: Swiss law (CC art. 50; CO art. 640) requires a genuine, identifiable postal address at which the company can be reached and where books and records can be produced; a pure letterbox or virtual mailbox without a tenancy and service agreement is insufficient for a green-coffee import AG; a serviced-office address with physical meeting facility, mail handling and data access is accepted in practice, subject to substance examination by tax, VAT and customs authorities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low, quantified at approximately 5-10% annually for a clean, licence-free specialty-coffee importer using documentary trade LCs; the likelihood rises to 30-50% when MROS/SECO flags, VAT or customs audits, or politically exposed counterparties trigger unannounced on-site attention.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of deed of incorporation, articles of association and annexes (standard AG, bilingual statutes)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss public notary of the canton of incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff (cantonal notarial fee schedule; benchmark CHF 1,000-1,500)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial register entry fee and Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB) publication
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal commercial register office and SHAB
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory maximum under SR 221.411 art. 12 (examination fee CHF 800) plus publication fee of approximately CHF 200

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance search and reservation fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal tariff (CHF 50 per reservation), valid for 6 months

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Federal Department of Justice and Police / Federal Commercial Register Portal
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Federal tariff (CHF 90 per filing, subject to indexation)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization of foreign corporate and identity documents (3-4 originals)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent foreign authorities under the Hague Apostille Convention of 1961 or Swiss diplomatic missions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (CHF 75-100 per document, plus consular service fees)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of statutes and supporting documents into the official register language (German or French)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator admitted in the canton of incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Swiss Translators Association (ASTTI) benchmark; flat fee CHF 500

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT pre-screening and sanctions hit-check report on directors, UBOs and three material coffee-origin counterparties
Bank share-capital deposit confirmation (Art. 632 OR) and account opening preparation
Registered office, virtual corporate seat and mail-forwarding service (first three months)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (CHF 1,800 per quarter for a trading SPV in Zurich or Zug)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Miscellaneous registry certified copies, courier and administrative handling
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal commercial register and service providers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under SR 221.411 art. 12 plus actual courier costs

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht) Art. 626 et seq. and Art. 629, 640, 641; Swiss Civil Code Art. 52; Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung) Art. 18
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association (Statuten) submitted via e-register or notarized filing
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital CHF 100,000; at least 20% (min. CHF 50,000) must be paid up in cash or specified assets before registration; confirmation of capital payment via bank or escrow account blocked in favour of the company required
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the Company be established as an Aktiengesellschaft under the Swiss Code of Obligations and do hereby adopt the Articles of Association presented to this Board. RESOLVED FURTHER: That the fully paid-up share capital as certified by the escrow account bank statement is accepted, and the registered office of the Company is fixed at the address stated in the Articles. RESOLVED FURTHER: That the persons named in the minutes are elected as the Board of Directors and the Managing Director, with authority to represent the Company singly, and any two officers are authorized to execute filings with the Commercial Register and all relevant licensing authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the Company Name and Verify Eligibility
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Commercial Register Office via the central name search portal (www.zefix.ch) and the Cantonal Commercial Register Office of Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform an online name availability search on ZEFIX. Submit a name reservation request stating the proposed corporate name, legal form (AG/SA), registered seat, and business purpose (import and distribution of specialty green coffee beans under ISIC 4631). The name must not mislead, impersonate, or infringe existing trademarks. Obtain a written preliminary clearance from the Cantonal Commercial Register.
required_dossiers: Fully executed name reservation form
Power of attorney for the applicant
Copy of founder passports or ID documents
Summary of business purpose in accordance with ISIC 4631
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit a revised name within 5 business days and provide evidence of distinctiveness and trade mark search clearance; request an administrative review by the Commercial Register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Notarize the Articles of Association and Incorporation Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss notary public authorized in Canton Zug and Cantonal Commercial Register Office of Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Swiss notary to prepare the public deed of incorporation incorporating the Articles of Association. Include the company name, corporate seat, authorized share capital, registered share categories, board composition, auditors (if required), and publishing requirements. Ensure the business purpose clause explicitly includes 'international wholesale distribution of unroasted green coffee beans, single-origin sourcing, and containerized trade logistics.' Sign the deed before the notary and obtain official notarization, then file the deed together with the signed Articles.
required_dossiers: Drafted Articles of Association
Notarized deed of incorporation
Declaration by the founders confirming contribution obligations
Bank escrow account statement evidencing payment of at least CHF 50,000
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correction notices from the notary or register must be cured by filing an addendum; if a material defect is identified, re-notarization of the corrected deed is required before re-submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open a Capital Escrow Account and Pay Up the Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss bank licensed by FINMA acting as a custodian of share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked bank account in the name of the future corporation (or a licensed third-party escrow account) with a Swiss bank. Deposit the paid-up minimum capital of CHF 50,000 from the founders' bank accounts, ensuring full traceability of funds. Obtain the bank certificate confirming the amount is irrevocably held at the disposal of the company and subject to authorized disbursement only after provisional registration.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening application
Certified copies of founder identification
Source of funds declaration for the capital deposit
Escrow agreement and bank certificate of blocked funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank certificate is queried, provide audited bank confirmation letters and refile within 5 business days; if capital is deemed insufficient, require an additional contribution prior to registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the First Board Resolution on Subscription, Registered Office, and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inaugural Board of Directors of the newly formed Aktiengesellschaft
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene an official board meeting. Record the board's acceptance of the full share subscription and paid-up capital, confirmation of the registered office address in the Canton of Zug, and election of the board chair, members, and managing director. Prepare signed minutes of the board resolution in the official corporate language (German or English with German translation if required by the Commercial Register). The resolution must be notarized to the extent required by Swiss law.
required_dossiers: Notice convening the initial board meeting
Signed board minutes containing the formal resolution
Acceptance letters from each elected director and officer
Swiss criminal record extracts and academic certificates for directors (if requested)
Standing lack-of-conflict declaration by each officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Register contests the regularity of the resolution, correct formal defects by executing a supplementary resolution and resubmit, or call an extraordinary general meeting to cure officer election irregularities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the Commercial Register Filing and Obtain Provisional Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the complete application package electronically via the Swiss e-register portal or through the notary. Attach the notarized deed, Articles of Association, board resolution, bank certificate, and identification of authorized signatories. Pay the registration fee and await the formal entry. The registration is published in the Swiss Official Gazette (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt) upon provisional entry.
required_dossiers: Fully completed commercial register application form
Notarized incorporation deed and Articles of Association
First board resolution minutes
Bank escrow certificate for paid-up share capital
Director identification and signatory specimen signatures
Proof of business address lease or registered office consent from property owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is queried or rejected, respond to the Commercial Register's comments within 10 business days, provide amended documents or declarations as requested, and pay any additional processing fee; appeal any final denial to the Cantonal Commercial Register Appeals Commission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Finalize Registration and Handle Post-Registration Tax and Infrastructural Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of Zurich/Zug, Cantonal Tax Administration of Zug, and Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon final registration, obtain the official extract from the Commercial Register and the company's identification number (UID). Forward the registration extract to the Federal Tax Administration for tax registration and corporate income tax assessment, and to the Swiss Social Security authorities for old age and survivors' insurance (AHV) employer registration. If importing green coffee beans, obtain an EORI number and register for Swiss customs tariff processing.
required_dossiers: Final commercial register extract
Company UID number allocation letter
Tax registration forms for cantonal and federal taxes
AHV insurance employer registration form
Customs EORI registration certificate (if importing/exporting)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a tax or customs registration is pending, file an interim declaration with the competent authority to avoid administrative penalties, and cure incomplete information by submitting supplementary corporate documents.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Department of Economic Affairs and Cantonal Food Safety Office (Kantonales Lebensmittelinspektorat Zug); Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (FSVO) for the primary food business notification
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registration of Food Business Premises (Lebensmittelunternehmen-Registrierung) — for warehouse and repacking site, not a full operating license

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (BAFU) and Cantonal Environmental Protection Office of Zug
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (no full EIA report required; registration under annex notification for low-risk storage of unprocessed agricultural goods)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge must comply with Annex 3.1 of the Water Protection Ordinance (GSchV); VOC emissions from any coffee processing or roasting equipment if incidental must comply with the Clean Air Ordinance (LRV) Section 12; green coffee bean storage waste handling must meet Annex of the Waste Ordinance (VVEA) with separate binning and disposal contracts

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire protection certificate from the Canton of Zug Fire Inspectorate confirming the warehouse and office premises comply with VKF fire safety regulations; structural load assessment by a Swiss licensed civil engineer for the racking and bean storage pallets; occupational safety clearance under the Federal Workplace Act (ArbG) and accident prevention regulations (SUVA) including first aid equipment and emergency exits; employees' insurance declaration submitted to SUVA

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC) – access via www.estyv.admin.ch and the 'Suisse eTax' portal for VAT filing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity obtains a Swiss business identification number (UID / Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) by registering with the Federal Statistical Office or, if establishing a branch or company, through the cantonal commercial registry. For VAT purposes, the taxpayer must file a VAT registration application with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration, in writing or via the official portal, indicating the effective date of liability. Registration is required before commencing taxable activities if the annual worldwide turnover exceeds the statutory threshold; non-resident entities may appoint a tax representative if no Swiss domicile or fixed establishment exists.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Switzerland. A Swiss AG is mandatorily subject to entity-level corporate income tax at federal, cantonal, and communal levels. Available elections include VAT group taxation (for closely linked persons), the option to allocate specific corporate tax attributes to capital contributions, and certain participation relief elections for qualifying dividend income under the participation deduction regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (VAT / MWST / TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual worldwide taxable turnover (excluding VAT) for mandatory VAT registration; voluntary registration may be permitted under certain conditions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API stamping, or continuous transaction control (CTC) mandate is currently enforced. Switzerland uses bilateral QR-bill and Swiss eBill interoperable standards for electronic invoicing. A valid VAT invoice must contain statutory particulars; electronic transmission is acceptable, but the taxpayer remains responsible for archival integrity and audit-ready storage.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to the export of goods to a foreign country, including specialty green coffee beans dispatched or transported by the supplier to a destination outside Switzerland, provided the export is evidenced by customs documents. Services directly connected to exported goods, such as freight and insurance, may also qualify for zero-rating where the recipient is established abroad or where the service strictly supports the cross-border movement of the goods. The exporter must record the export in the VAT return and maintain proof of export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (customs-approved proof of export)
Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document (sea, air, road, or rail)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank payment evidence demonstrating the export proceeds received from the foreign buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Swiss Federal Tax Administration can retrospectively reclaim zero-rated VAT plus statutory interest if export documentation is missing, incomplete, or inconsistent. In cases of fraud or negligent misrepresentation, the limitation period extends to 10 years (ordinarily 5 years), and civil penalties may be imposed up to 50% of the evaded tax or up to CHF 500,000 for willful VAT offenses, without prejudice to separate customs penalties and criminal sanctions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB; Schweizerische Nationalbank / Banque nationale suisse), with prudential and AML supervision by the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA), trade policy coordination by the State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF), and balance-of-payments statistics administered by the SNB.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: CHF is fully convertible with no exchange-control regime and no legal distinction between current-account and capital-account transactions for residents or non-residents. Profit remittance is unrestricted: dividends may be repatriated freely subject to the 35% Swiss withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer), which is refundable or reduced under applicable double-tax treaties, including the Swiss-EU withholding tax agreement and unilateral Swiss-EU dividend tax relief. No prior Central Bank authorization is required for capital contributions, trade settlements, shareholder loans, or distributions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Switzerland imposes no statutory surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation deadline for export receipts. Exporters may freely hold and deploy foreign-currency proceeds. The only obligations are statistical and registration-type: threshold-based SNB balance-of-payments surveys, FINMA reporting for regulated entities, and Federal Customs Administration declarations where the commodity transit regime is used; none requires converting foreign exchange into CHF.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital escrow deposit account (Sperrkonto for the AG incorporation) followed by a CHF operational current account and USD/EUR multi-currency trade settlement accounts
Operational CHF/USD/EUR account with a dedicated commodity trade finance desk and documentary credit capabilities; capital deposit account also offered
Operational CHF/USD account for trade settlements and short-term liquidity
Operational account through the local cooperative branch network; limited commodity trade finance product suite

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High as a supplementary treasury layer: Swiss FINMA-supervised fintech payment firms operating under the Art. 1b Banking Act fintech license, or AMLA-registered financial intermediaries, offer API-driven multi-currency accounts, automated FX execution, and straight-through processing. Low as the sole primary banking rail for offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Estonia, Lithuania, UK): they lack direct SIC/SNB settlement membership, rely on correspondent nesting, and are not passportable into Switzerland; they are acceptable only as ring-fenced non-CHF wallets for minor origin-country payments.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance is effectively mandatory for at least one director and for each ultimate beneficial owner, or alternatively an in-person interview conducted before an authorized Swiss notary, fiduciary, or bank-appointed representative. Remote 'Video-Ident' is legally permitted under FINMA Circular 2016/07 for low-risk retail clients, but Tier-1 Swiss banks retain absolute discretion to require a live interview at a Swiss branch for any non-resident corporate structure; for this CH_AG a branch interview with the CFO and UBO is the compliance-safe assumption. No general right to fully remote onboarding exists for a trading stock corporation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident corporate shareholders held through a multi-tiered holding chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified excerpt from the Swiss commercial register (Handelsregister); complete share register (Aktienbuch); notarized Articles of Association and board resolutions on shareholding; UBO declaration pursuant to Art. 4 AMLA on the standard bank form; recent apostilled and translated excerpt of the foreign parent's corporate registry.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flags from green-coffee invoice over- or under-pricing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Benchmark-derived price verification using the ICE Arabica 'C' contract and ICO composite indicator; signed purchase and sale contracts specifying Incoterms; bills of lading, customs declarations, SGS/verifier weight and moisture certificates; warehouse receipts and container tracking records; payment-to-invoice reconciliation ledger.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-wealth opacity for the initial shareholder capital injection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements of the contributing shareholder for the last three years; sworn source-of-wealth statement; bank reference letter from the remitting institution; tax residency certificate and corporate good-standing evidence; SWIFT MT103 history evidencing accumulation of funds within a regulated banking system.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or embargo exposure of coffee origin counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written sanctions policy with SECO, OFAC, and UN screening logs for all counterparties; end-beneficiary and re-export attestations; country eligibility matrix confirming sanctioned origins are excluded; external Swiss legal opinion where transit risk exists; contractual force-majeure and sanctions clauses.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex multi-jurisdiction payable chain (origin exporter, Swiss entity, EU roaster)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group treasury policy and intercompany agreements; OECD transfer pricing documentation for the marketing and distribution functions; FX hedging policy and netting schedules; full invoice-to-settlement audit trail; periodic internal AML compliance review attestation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: shareholder transfers CHF/EUR/USD via SIC, EURO SIC, or SWIFT using MT103 (or ISO 20022 pacs.008) with payment purpose code 'CAPC' (capital contribution) and instruction text 'Einzahlung Aktienkapital'; the receiving bank credits the escrow account or operational account; verification comprises notarized capital call resolutions, the bank's blocked-account confirmation (Sperrkonto-Bestätigung) for the incorporation deposit, a capital payment statement filed with the commercial-register notary, and retained source-of-funds documentation for every inbound leg.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier prepayments and spot settlements are executed via SWIFT MT103 in USD/EUR through the UBS or ZKB correspondent clearing networks; documentary settlements for containerized specialty green coffee use irrevocable documentary letters of credit (SWIFT MT700/MT707) with the Swiss bank as issuing bank; CHF and EUR disbursements additionally clear through SIC and SEPA respectively; FX settlement is hedged and cleared via CLS where the counterparty bank is a CLS member; intercompany and profit repatriation flows are contractual and backed by audited transfer pricing documentation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forward contracts on USD/CHF, EUR/CHF, and USD/EUR
FX swaps for liquidity management and rollover of trade positions
Cross-currency swaps for long-term commodity trade financing
Vanilla FX options, including collars and protective puts on USD/CHF for green-coffee procurement

Non-deliverable forwards, permitted only restrictively for non-convertible origin-market currencies where local delivery in CHF or USD is legally prohibited; NDFs on CHF are unnecessary and generally not offered given full convertibility

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and management report presented to shareholders at the Annual General Meeting (AGM)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders (AGM); no filing with a public registry for non-listed AG unless required by the cantonal tax authority in the annual corporate tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the balance sheet date; for a calendar-year financial year, the AGM must be held no later than 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to approve financial statements can trigger a formal invitation from the commercial registry to regularize; persistent compliance default may lead to administrative strike-off after insolvency or abandonment of the company. Board members may become personally liable for damage caused by delayed reporting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (federal, cantonal, and municipal direct tax) including signed financial statements, depreciation schedules, and shareholder/equity reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration representing the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) and the municipal tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 31 March for calendar-year companies; deadline extension to 31 August is available upon justified request to the cantonal tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest on tax due at approximately 3.5%–4.5% per annum; late-filing surcharge of up to 30% of the assessed tax for negligent or intentional delay; repeated non-filing can lead to administrative penal proceedings under the Swiss Federal Direct Tax Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual value-added tax (VAT) return and final VAT reconciliation for the calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA) – VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of the reporting period; for annual reporting with a calendar-year VAT period, the filing is due by 28 February of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of up to 3% of the unpaid VAT amount; default interest; proven VAT evasion is punishable with a fine of up to CHF 20,000 or imprisonment under Article 31 of the Swiss Value Added Tax Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual employer payroll and social security contribution statement (AHV/IV/EO), including annual verification of pension fund participation (BVG/Occupational Benefit Plan)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Social Insurance Office (FSIO) via the competent cantonal compensation fund (Ausgleichskasse)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the end of the wage settlement period; employers with a calendar-year payroll must usually file by 31 January of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative surcharge on overdue employer contributions; coercive payment order if unresolved; failure to maintain mandatory pension insurance is a criminal offence under the Swiss Federal Law on Occupational Old-Age, Survivors' and Disability Insurance (BVG).

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An ordinary (full) statutory audit is mandatory if the AG exceeds two of these three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total of CHF 20 million, turnover of CHF 40 million, and an annual average of 250 full-time employees. A limited audit is required for companies failing to meet ordinary audit thresholds unless shareholders unanimously waive the audit entirely; such waiver is permitted only for companies with fewer than 10 full-time employees on annual average and is subject to the consent of all shareholders.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (Articles 957–962) as the primary statutory framework; Swiss GAAP FER is the generally accepted financial reporting framework for management reporting; IFRS is permitted as an enhanced accounting standard for listed or finance-oriented entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland maintains no central annual beneficial-ownership filing. The AG must keep an internal register of ultimate beneficial owners for Anti-Money Laundering Act compliance. The board or compliance officer performs an annual confirmation review, signs a dated internal confirmation, and updates the register after any transfer of shares, voting rights, or control. In case of a share transfer affecting ownership above the applicable threshold, the register must be updated within the ordinary statutory amendment cycle and the annual audit file must include the UBO reconciliation. On demand by the cantonal commercial registry or tax authority, the register must be produced; failure to maintain it is subject to the AMLA penalty provisions.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CHF 1,200–5,000 per year (approximately USD 1,400–5,600 per year)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: CHF 6,000–40,000 per year (approximately USD 7,000–45,000 per year) depending on company size, number of shareholders, and audit scope

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Swiss federal statutory corporate income tax rate is 8.5% on taxable profit after federal tax, equivalent to 7.83% on a pre-tax basis. Combined federal, cantonal and municipal profit tax rates for an Aktiengesellschaft range from approximately 11.9% in lower-tax cantons such as Zug to approximately 21.0% in higher-tax cantons such as Zurich. For a Zug-based specialty green coffee distribution AG, the aggregate statutory effective rate is generally between 11.9% and 14.4%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Swiss tax law does not provide a general statutory tax holiday for coffee trading companies. Available reliefs include: participation relief for qualifying dividend and capital-gain income; patent box deductions of up to 90% on qualifying IP income; R&D super-deductions of up to an additional 50% of eligible Swiss R&D expenditure, capped per canton; and cantonal capital-tax relief on qualifying participations and internal reserves. A standard specialty green coffee bean importer cannot rely on special IP boxes unless it owns patents, plant-variety rights, or proprietary processing/logistics software generating separately identifiable income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Swiss corporate income tax return for legal entities, combining the federal direct tax declaration and the cantonal/municipal tax schedules issued by the competent cantonal tax administration. The official return is filed on the relevant cantonal form for Aktiengesellschaften, e.g., Zurich NOVA-File or Zug 'Steuererklärung juristische Personen', and electronically through the canton's secure e-portal or via approved e-filing software; OECD CbCR schedules are filed through the Swiss Federal Tax Administration's dedicated portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The AG must file within 30 days of the official tax return form being issued by the cantonal tax office. For calendar-year accounts, the commercial filing date in most cantons is 31 March of the following year; some cantons set 30 June. For non-calendar fiscal years, the deadline is generally six months after fiscal year-end. Extensions may be applied for in writing; late-filing extension requests do not suspend payment obligations on assessed provisional instalments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1a / Line 12 - Company identification and general particulars
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal form, name, CHE-UID/VAT registration number, registered seat, purpose, share capital, board members, signatories, auditors, and business address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate the legal seat in Switzerland and any actual place of management. Non-resident shareholders are not entered individually, but the UID and share-register data must be reconcilable with the foreign beneficial ownership declaration on request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 / Line 20 - Commercial profit per statutory annual financial statements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit before tax as shown in the audited Swiss GAAP FER, IFRS, or statutory balance sheet and income statement, including prior-year adjustments and corrections of earlier assessments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident-owned distribution AG, the reported profit must be consistent with the transfer-pricing documentation; a full-risk coffee distributor is expected to earn the arm's length return for its functions, assets and risks.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Additions and deductions required by Swiss tax law: non-deductible representations, tax penalties, hidden-reserve releases, participation-relief deductions, patent-box deductions, R&D super-deductions, and loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident parent should ensure the Swiss entity's intercompany expense claims are fully documented and that any recharacterized dividends or hidden contributions are reflected under the applicable corporate tax schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 4a - Domestic and foreign participation income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report of dividends, liquidation surpluses, capital gains and share-income qualifying for participation relief; applicable holding thresholds of at least 10% of nominal capital or profit shares.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Swiss AG merely holds an intermediary coffee-purchasing subsidiary, participation relief must be claimed at the Swiss level; the non-resident shareholder's residence country remains responsible for its own repatriation taxation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 6 / Annex TP - Transfer pricing and intercompany transactions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of all material transactions with foreign and domestic related parties: green coffee purchase prices, commission fees, freight, insurance, demurrage, warehousing, interest on shareholder loans, management fees, royalties, and year-end balances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the functional-risk analysis, comparables benchmark, contractual documentation, and a statement that the Swiss entity retains pricing risk and active distribution functions; a low-risk commissionaire profile without employees or decision-making will be disregarded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable equity capital for cantonal/municipal capital tax: paid-in share capital, statutory and voluntary reserves, retained earnings, and unrealized gains after declared adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The capital tax is computed on the Swiss AG's net equity at fiscal year-end; non-resident shareholders have no direct filing obligation, but capital increases or loans treated as equity will increase the cantonal capital-tax base.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a reminder and potentially discretionary assessment by the tax authority. Under Art. 174 DBG, culpable failure to file the federal tax return can result in a procedure fine of up to CHF 10,000, plus cantonal surcharges and late-payment interest on State and cantonal taxes generally at 3.5% per annum. Deliberate false declarations constitute tax evasion under Art. 175 DBG, punishable by a fine equal to the tax evaded and, for repeated or fraudulent conduct, fines of up to 300% of the evaded tax; tax fraud under Art. 176 DBG carries imprisonment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal_note: The same annual return is used for federal, cantonal and municipal profit/capital tax. Separate Swiss withholding-tax returns are filed monthly or quarterly for dividend distributions and 35% federal withholding tax remittance.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Swiss federal withholding tax on dividends is 35%. For a non-resident shareholder that is not entitled to treaty relief, 35% is final and must be withheld and remitted by the AG. Under an applicable double-taxation agreement, the rate may be reduced to 0%, 5%, 10%, or 15% depending on the ownership structure and specific treaty; the most common corporate participation relief requires beneficial ownership and a direct shareholding of at least 10% of voting rights.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, the foreign beneficial owner must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its residence state and submit it, together with the applicable Swiss withholding-tax relief form, share-register extract, certificate of incorporation and a beneficial-ownership declaration, to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration through the paying agent or directly. The FTA will examine whether the DTA conditions, including substance and residence, are satisfied. If relief is granted, the dividend may be remitted net at the treaty rate; if not granted before payment, the full 35% is withheld and the shareholder must file a reclaim claim with the FTA within the treaty limitation period, usually three years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Switzerland does not impose statutory withholding tax on royalties or ordinary arm's length intercompany interest paid to non-residents. Interest on domestically issued bonds and certain bank deposit interest remains subject to 35% withholding tax. Therefore, royalty payments for coffee trademarks, proprietary logistics software, or processing technology, and interest on shareholder loans funded by genuine debt, may be paid without Swiss source withholding. However, if the royalty or interest is not arm's length, the excess will be treated as a constructive dividend subject to 35% Swiss withholding tax. Under most Swiss DTAs, the residual source-country rate for royalties is 0%, and for interest 0% or a reduced rate, provided the recipient is the beneficial owner.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Swiss transfer-pricing documentation is required where the group's consolidated turnover exceeds CHF 50 million or where the Swiss entity's cross-border intercompany transactions exceed CHF 5 million per year; OECD Country-by-Country Reporting applies when group consolidated revenue is CHF 900 million or more. A coffee distribution AG below these thresholds must still evidence the pricing in its invoices, contracts, purchase confirmations, bills of lading, and financing agreements if challenged.
